sentences.text:
This is an Appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short, "M.V. Act") by the Insurance Company of the offending Truck against the Judgment and Award dated 25.02.2015 passed by learned Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Gondia ("MACT" for short) in Claim Petition No.98/2008, holding the Appellant and Truck Owner jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs. 18,10,000/- with interest @ 7% p.a.
2.
The aforesaid Claim Petition was filed by the Respondent nos.1 and 2, who are the mother and the Son of deceased Jaikumar.

According to the Claimants, deceased Jaikumar died in the motor vehicular accident dated 11th March, 2007 while he was travelling on the motorcycle from Sakoli to Gondia and the offending Truck which was insured with the Appellant-Insurance Company gave dash to the motorcycle from the opposite direction.
The Claimants' claim compensation of Rs.25,00,000/-.
The Claim Petition was contested by the Appellant by filing Written Statement.
The learned Tribunal, upon appreciating the evidence on record, passed by the impugned Judgment and Award.

3. It is submitted by the learned Advocate for the Appellant - Insurance Company that, the Driver of the offending Truck was examined before the learned Tribunal to show that, the 3 fa688.2016.odt accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the motorcycle by the deceased.
The learned Tribunal did not appreciate the evidence in its correct perspective and recorded the finding that, the Truck Driver was responsible for the accident.
He submits that, the learned Tribunal has wrongly applied the multiplier of 18 instead of 17 while calculating the compensation.
He submits that, the Appeal be allowed.
4. It is submitted by the learned Advocate of the Claimants that, the Crime was registered against the Truck Driver for the said accident.

Though the Insurance Company examined the Truck Driver,
it failed to prove that, the accident took place due to negligence of the deceased.
He fairly concedes that, the wrong multiplier was applied by the learned Tribunal.
5. With the assistance of the learned Advocates for both the sides, perused the papers on record.
There is no dispute in respect of the death of Jaikumar in the motor vehicular accident dated 11th March, 2007.
Undisputedly, the offence was registered with the Gondia Police Station for the said accident against the Driver of the Truck, which was insured with the Appellant - Insurance Company.
The Appellant - Insurance Company examined Truck Driver, as Witness No.1.
He deposed that, he was driving the Truck in slow speed and the road was having heavy traffic.
The 4 fa688.2016.odt motorcycle was coming in high speed and dashed to the Truck.
He deposed that, he was acquitted by the Criminal Court.
The motorcycle got slipped and came under the Truck.
He was driving the Truck of its proper side.
The said witness was cross-examined by the Advocate for the Claimants.
It has come in the cross- examination that, the Truck was having passing of 9 Tons and he did not stop his truck on the spot of accident.
The Police papers brought on record by the Claimants before the learned Tribunal comprises of the spot panchanama at Exhibit-37.
There is mention in the said spot panchanama that, the Truck Driver fled from the spot.
The spot panchanama shows that, the road on which the accident took place was 25 feet wide.

Witness No.1 of the Appellant - Insurance Company in his evidence has taken two contrary stands.
At one point, he deposed that, the motorcycle came in high speed and gave dash to the Truck and on the other side, he deposed that, the motorcycle slipped and came under the Truck.
This evidence do not conclusively establish that, the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the motorcycle.
The material on record gives rise to the only conclusion that, the accident was the result of rash and negligent driving of the Truck, which was insured by the Insurance Company.
The learned Tribunal 5 fa688.2016.odt has considered this aspect in para 10 of the impugned Judgment.

The said paragraph is reproduced below:-
"Evidence of petitioner No. 1 is well supported by the documentary evidence i.e. FIR Exh. 35, Spot Panchanama Exh. 37 clearly show that accident took place due to rash and negligent driving of the respondent No. 3.
There is no dispute that deceased died due to injuries sustained in the accident.
Post Mortem report is at Exh. 38.
Evidence of respondent No. 3 is nothing, but to save liability of respondents.
Respondent No. 3 not filed written 10 statement.
He was prosecuted by policy.
He has stated that he acquitted by the Court.
Acquittal by criminal court cannot be a ground to deny the case of petitioners".

6. In view of the above, no fault can be found with the observations of the learned Tribunal that, the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the Truck and no interference is called for on the said aspect.

7. As regards the ground of applying wrong multiplier is concerned, the Advocate for the Claimants fairly concedes that, for the age of deceased as 27, the multiplier as per Chart in case Sarla Verma and others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr. AIR 2009 Supreme Court 3104, would be 17 and not 18.

sentences.text:
Thus, the amount of compensation is recalculated as under:-
6 fa688.2016.odt Yearly Income Rs. 1,50,000 (Minus) 1/3rd Deduction 50,000 Rs.
1,00,000 Multiplier 17 as per age of deceased X 17 Rs. 17,00,000 Plus Funeral Expenses Rs. 2,000 On all other counts Rs. 8,000 Total Rs.17,10,000 8.

In view of the above, the amount of total compensation is modified to the extent of Rs.17,10,000/-
instead of Rs.18,10,000/-, which is computed by the learned Tribunal.
The rest of the operative order of the learned Tribunal stands intact.
Record and proceedings be sent back to the learned Tribunal.
9. The amount deposited by the Insurance Company in this Court is permitted to be withdrawn by the Claimants, as per the modified Award along with accrued interest.
The remaining amount, if any, after disbursement to the Claimants, be refunded with accrued interest to the Insurance Company.
10. The amount of compensation be deposited in the account of Claimants.
The Claimants shall file supporting documents before the Registrar (Judicial) at the time of withdrawal.
